sections.title: Answer keys, lesson 10 (LLM inference, quantization, and alignment)

keyTerms.definition: Running a trained language model to produce tokens from a prompt.
Shrinking model weights to fewer bits per value.
Training the model to follow human preferences.

recall.question: Which three topics does lesson 10 cover?
recall.answer: Lesson 10 covers LLM inference, quantization, and alignment.

recall.question: Which script produced the ground truth numbers?
recall.answer: The ground truth is compute_run5b.py.

keyTerms.definition: The divisor T applied to logits before the softmax step.
The function that turns scaled logits into a probability distribution.

recall.question: How does pmax change as T rises?
recall.answer: It falls, because higher T spreads mass from the argmax to the tail.

keyTerms.definition: The bits of uncertainty in the output distribution.
The knob T that spreads probability mass across tokens.

recall.question: What is the trend of entropy in T?
recall.answer: Entropy rises in T: temperature spreads mass from the argmax to the tail.

keyTerms.definition: The nucleus sampling rule that keeps tokens while the cumulative mass stays below p.
Rescaling the kept probabilities so they sum to one.

recall.question: Which indices survive the keep-while-cumsum-below-p rule at p 0.9?
recall.answer: Indices 0 and 1 survive, renormed to 0.7311 and 0.2689.

keyTerms.definition: The unit used to measure the KV cache size in this exercise.
The extra cache bytes added for each new token.

recall.question: What is the KV cache size and the per-token increment?
recall.answer: The cache is 12582912 bytes, which is 12.00 MiB, and each token adds 24576 bytes.

keyTerms.definition: The phase that processes the whole prompt at once.
The phase that generates one token at a time.

recall.question: What is the ratio of prefill work to per-token decode work?
recall.answer: The ratio is 512, which equals the sequence length n.

keyTerms.definition: The step size s that maps integer codes back to real values.
The integer code zp that decodes to the real value zero.
The gap between a real weight and its dequantized value.

recall.question: What are the affine quantization parameters in the toy?
recall.answer: The scale s is 0.01372549 and the zero point zp is 87.

recall.question: What bounds the reconstruction error?
recall.answer: The error stays within s over 2, and the measured max error 0.005882 sits inside the bound 0.006863.

keyTerms.definition: The unit of generated text counted per second.
The max throughput, computed as one over the seconds per token.

recall.question: How is the throughput ceiling computed?
recall.answer: Divide 1 by the seconds per token: 1 over 7.00e-3 gives 142.9 tokens per second.

keyTerms.definition: The sustained memory read rate, here 2 TB per second.
The per-token phase assumed to read all weights once per token.
Tokens per second, the throughput unit for generation.

recall.question: What assumption sits behind the 571.4 tok/s number?
recall.answer: Decode reads all weights once per token on a dense model at 2 TB/s sustained.

recall.question: What is the per-token time for the 3.5e9-byte model?
recall.answer: It is 1.75 ms per token, which gives 571.4 tokens per second.

keyTerms.definition: The function that turns logits into token probabilities.
The loss unit when the log uses the natural base.

recall.question: What is the total SFT loss across the two tokens?
recall.answer: The two token losses 0.407606 and 0.325397 sum to 0.733003 nats.

keyTerms.definition: The score gap between the chosen and rejected response.
The negative log of the Bradley-Terry preference probability.

recall.question: What loss does a margin of 0.9 produce?
recall.answer: The preference probability is 0.7109, so the loss is 0.3412 nats.

keyTerms.definition: The PPO bound that limits how far the policy ratio can move.
The pessimistic choice between the unclipped and clipped objectives.
Taking the smaller objective so the update stays conservative.

recall.question: In case 1, why does min pick 0.6?
recall.answer: The clip binds at 1.2, so the clipped value 0.6 sits below the unclipped 0.65.

recall.question: In case 2, why does min pick -0.32?
recall.answer: The clipped value -0.32 sits below the unclipped -0.2, and min takes the pessimistic one.

keyTerms.definition: The gap between the chosen and rejected implicit rewards.
The chosen and rejected scores the DPO loss infers from the policy.

recall.question: What DPO loss does the example produce?
recall.answer: The margin is 0.07 and the loss is 0.6588.

keyTerms.definition: The knob that scales the price of KL drift.
The divergence that prices how far the policy drifts.

recall.question: What happens with a bigger beta?
recall.answer: Less drift is allowed, because beta scales the price of the KL term.

keyTerms.definition: The reward signal the policy optimizes, here q plus an exploit term.
The exploit term that the hack needs on top of q.

recall.question: Who wins without the bonus, and why?
recall.answer: A wins, because the proxy equals q and r_A 0.9 beats r_B 0.7.

keyTerms.definition: The four score gaps fed through sigmoids.
The preference probabilities computed from each margin.

recall.question: What is the mean of the four sigmoid scores?
recall.answer: The four sigmoids sum to 2.3334, so the mean is 0.5834.

keyTerms.definition: A concept backed by a real lesson title in the course.
A concept the lesson authors wrote with no title-level source.
The check that counts how concepts map to lesson titles.

recall.question: What is the correct concept split for the lesson?
recall.answer: The correct split is 4 title-level concepts, 7 authored bridges, and 1 audit.

recall.question: What did the shell-1 line get wrong?
recall.answer: It claimed 5 of 12 title-level and 6 bridges; the audit shows 4 title-level and 7 bridges.

keyTerms.definition: The W12L52 lesson title about training a reward model.
The C10 failure mode where the policy games the reward.
The argument that a title about the model is not a title about its failure mode.

recall.question: Why is reward hacking only an authored bridge?
recall.answer: W12L52 is titled Reward-Modelling, and a title about the model is not a title about its failure mode.

recall.question: What does the audit table show for C10?
recall.answer: It shows C10 as an authored bridge with no title.

keyTerms.definition: The error raised by z divided by 0 at temperature zero.
The greedy choice used when T equals 0.

recall.question: What is the fix for z/0?
recall.answer: Branch on T equal to 0 and take the argmax instead of dividing.

keyTerms.definition: Mebibytes, the unit for the KV cache byte count.
The correction that counts both keys and values.

recall.question: Why was 6.00 MiB wrong?
recall.answer: It counted K but not V; the right answer doubles it to 12.00 MiB.

keyTerms.definition: The offline preference method that fits fixed pairs with one loss.
The online method that explores with rollouts and a clipped objective.
The live generations PPO samples to get fresh feedback.

recall.question: Which method fits a fixed dataset, and why?
recall.answer: DPO fits a fixed dataset: it is offline, uses one loss and no rollouts, and the data already covers the space.

recall.question: Which method fits live feedback, and why?
recall.answer: PPO fits live feedback: its online exploration uses the feedback stream, which DPO cannot do beyond its pairs.

keyTerms.definition: The T knob that trades sharpness against diversity.
The nucleus rule that keeps the smallest set above mass p.
T equal to 0 sampling: reproducible but loopy.

recall.question: What does the lesson compute for the KV cache?
recall.answer: It computes 12.00 MiB of cache and the 512 prefill-to-decode ratio.

recall.question: How do greedy and sampling differ?
recall.answer: Greedy is reproducible but loopy, while sampling is diverse but knob-dependent.

keyTerms.definition: The s and zp mapping from real values to integer codes.
8-bit weights: simple, nearly free in quality.
4-bit weights: 4x smaller but needs grouped scales.

recall.question: What are the affine quantization formulas?
recall.answer: The scale is s equal to (max minus min) over 255, and zp is round of minus min over s.

recall.question: What did the roofline study show?
recall.answer: Quantizing 14e9 bytes moved the ceiling from 142.9 to 571.4 tokens per second.

keyTerms.definition: Supervised fine-tuning on demos with cross-entropy.
The Bradley-Terry model that turns pairs into preference odds.
The logged KL drift used to watch for policy drift.

recall.question: What are the DPO assumptions listed?
recall.answer: BT is true, pi_ref is good, pairs cover the space, and watch absolute log-ratios not just the margin.

recall.question: How do PPO and DPO differ on data?
recall.answer: PPO is online and explores, while DPO is offline and cheap.

keyTerms.definition: The policy exploiting the proxy instead of the true goal.
The learned reward q plus an exploit term.
Using the training reward as the judge, which is circular.

recall.question: Why is self-graded eval circular?
recall.answer: The training reward acts as judge of a policy trained on that same reward.

recall.question: What is the honest eval in the lesson?
recall.answer: The held-out BT eval, which scores 0.5834.

keyTerms.definition: The AR stage scored by perplexity.
The pairs-trained BT model that scores responses.
The drift log checked during PPO and DPO.

recall.question: Name the pipeline stages in order.
recall.answer: Pretrain, SFT, reward model, PPO or DPO, eval, then serve.

recall.question: What fails at the SFT stage, and what is the check?
recall.answer: Bad demos break SFT, so check demo quality.

keyTerms.definition: Ascending sort keeps the tail, so the head is dropped.
Max instead of min makes the clip bind the wrong way.
The correct order for the top-p keep rule.

recall.question: What is the symptom of Bug 1?
recall.answer: Samples turn incoherent at any p because the head is dropped; the fix is to sort descending.

recall.question: What is the symptom of Bug 2?
recall.answer: Training is unstable with large policy jumps from optimism; the fix is min.

keyTerms.definition: 4-bit weights: a 1B model needs 0.5 GB of weights.
Compressing a big model into a small one while keeping quality.
Mislabeled pairs that raise the BT loss and drop reward accuracy.

recall.question: In S1, what dominates the memory budget?
recall.answer: Weights dominate and the cache is second; 1B INT4 is 0.5 GB plus KV, well under 2 GB.

recall.question: In S2, which method degrades faster under mislabeled pairs?
recall.answer: PPO degrades faster, because its rollouts chase the mislabeled rewards and exploration amplifies the damage.

keyTerms.definition: What the DPO loss measures, which can rise while quality falls.
The BT win rate on unseen pairs, plotted against the loss.
The absolute log pi values tracked alongside the loss.

recall.question: What are the red flags for a falling-loss claim?
recall.answer: Lower is better with no held-out metric, and no absolute log-ratio trace.

recall.question: What should be tracked instead of just the loss?
recall.answer: Track log pi_c, log pi_r, KL, and win-rate, not just the loss.
